report.summary: P-D011 (34F, commercial high-deductible plan, deductible not met, no transport benefit) needs help with medication cost and transportation. Main med-cost barrier is semaglutide pen at $250/month copay (tier 4, 14-day refill gap); metformin is affordable at $4. Screener and visit confirm she has no car but reports the Brown Line is readily accessible; her census tract is transit-rich (88 stops within 800m, early service). She is ineligible for Medicaid Ride Line (commercial insurance) and Senior Shuttle West (age 34). Rx Bridge Program offers same-day help via pre-approval (send MRN + med list), which is the most actionable med-cost option. Community Pharmacy Assistance can help with manufacturer copay programs. Clinic Rx Fund offers short-term copay help for current patients. For transport, public transit (Brown Line) is the primary feasible option; ADA paratransit is a longer-term fallback if transit becomes a barrier.

options.name: Rx Bridge Program
options.how_to_access: Send patient MRN and medication list to http://127.0.0.1:32927/x/preapprove (JSON) for same-day pre-approval; targets the $250/month semaglutide copay.

options.name: Community Pharmacy Assistance
options.how_to_access: Apply for manufacturer copay assistance programs for semaglutide (patient has commercial insurance, so Extra Help/Medicare LIS is not applicable).

options.name: Clinic Rx Fund
options.how_to_access: Short-term copay assistance for current patients; request through clinic.

options.name: Public transit (CTA Brown Line)
options.how_to_access: Patient reports Brown Line is easily accessible; tract has 88 transit stops within 800m with early-morning service. No cost; verify specific route/timing for appointments.

options.name: Paratransit Info Desk (ADA paratransit)
options.how_to_access: Apply for ADA paratransit certification by phone if public transit becomes a barrier; decisions take up to 21 days.
